descriptionChirho: One who is materially destitute or in a state of economic poverty, often as a social class deserving justice and compassion.
One who suffers distress, oppression, or misery, emphasizing the experiential condition of suffering rather than mere economic lack.
One who is meek or humble in disposition before God, denoting a spiritual or moral quality rather than an external condition.
Feminine form used as a vocative or epithet, typically addressing a personified city (e.g., Jerusalem/Zion) as a suffering, storm-tossed figure.
